Civil Police in Água Clara, Mato Grosso do Sul, arrested five men in a
drug-trafficking investigation. The operation began on the night of
Wednesday 4 November after an anonymous tip said a vehicle was being used to
sell drugs in the city. The tip named a white VW Gol in the Jardim das
Palmeiras neighbourhood. Military police found the car and the driver tried
to flee, but was caught after a chase of a few blocks.

In the car officers found a portion of a cocaine-like substance, and at the
driver's home they seized portions of marijuana, a precision scale, packaging
material and cash. At a second address used to store drugs, teams found 59
tablets of a marijuana-like substance weighing about 54 kg. The fuller
police account says two men aged 18 and 20 were caught red-handed at that
address. A third suspect, 22, was caught with about 500 g of marijuana and
a precision scale. Police also recovered a bag holding 19 portions of
cocaine of about 120 g, which they said the first suspect had discarded during
the stop. A fifth man, 28, who had an outstanding warrant for drug
trafficking, was also arrested. Alongside the drugs, officers seized a car,
a motorcycle, three precision scales, three phones, packaging and about R$ 250
in cash.

Four of the five were booked in flagrante for drug trafficking and association
for trafficking, while the fifth was captured on a court order. The joint
operation was carried out by the Civil Police and the Military Police.
Those involved were taken to the Água Clara Civil Police station for legal
measures.

A Sohag Criminal Court sentenced three men to death by hanging for possessing
hashish with intent to traffic and holding a scalpel without legal cause in
Egypt's El Maragha district, ordering them to pay costs and confiscating the
seized items. The three defendants were listed as M.A, 35, and M.M, 25,
both holders of industrial-arts diplomas, and A.A, 41, who did not work. A
second account named them as Mohamed Ismail Abdel-Lah Mohamed, Mohamed Mohamed
Farghali Ahmed and Essam Ismail Abdel-Lah Mohamed, all from El Ghanayem district
in Assiut Governorate.

A chemical laboratory report found the seized brown material was hashish resin,
divided into three lots of 80, 150 and 50 pieces — 280 pieces in total — plus a
plastic bag with traces of the drug. The case goes back to November 2025,
when officers of the General Administration for Drug Control's Sohag branch
arrested the defendants after the Public Prosecution authorised a search of the
first defendant. Prosecutors charged the three with possessing hashish for
trafficking and using cars to transport and promote the drugs.

After the investigation the Public Prosecution referred the case to the Sohag
Criminal Court for trial. The judgment was delivered by a panel headed by
counsellor Hamdy Abdel-Aziz, with counsellors Mohy Abou Kreisha and Amr Mekki
and clerks Taha Hussein and Magid Amin. After the hearing the court sent
the case to the Grand Mufti for a religious opinion on the death sentences and,
once his opinion arrived, issued its final judgment unanimously.

report.body:
Catalan police arrested seven men aged 29 to 55 on 1 October 2026 at an
industrial warehouse in Cabanes, Girona, on suspicion of links to a
drug-trafficking organisation. Four of them were placed in provisional
prison without bail and the other three with bail, according to the Catalan
public broadcaster. The Mossos said the investigation was carried out by
the narcotics group of their criminal investigation unit in Sant Feliu de
Llobregat. The seven detainees were brought before the Civil and
Instruction Section of the Court of Instance at Figueres. Police said the
investigation remained open and did not rule out further arrests.

Officers seized 8,025 kg of hashish from the warehouse, the Mossos said.
The hashish was hidden in large raffia sacks filled with rubber crumb, a method
used to make detection at police or customs checks harder. The Mossos
valued the seized drugs at more than 16.2 million euros on the illicit market. La Razón reported that the haul was more than half (53.9%) of the roughly
14.9 tonnes of hashish seized in 2026 up to 1 October. Inside the warehouse
officers found a firearm in one of the detainees' vans.

The investigation started in June 2026, when Mossos stopped a van carrying
nearly 2,400 kg of hashish in Viladecans, Barcelona, and later traced the drug
to the Cabanes warehouse. A court in Gavà initially handled that earlier
vehicle case. Surveillance in early October showed people replacing
vehicles' number plates with others fixed with cable ties and an articulated
lorry entering the warehouse. Officers entered and found seven people
unloading pallets from the trailer to load the hashish into vans for
distribution. The warehouse was almost empty and had no sign of any
business or residential use, which officers said confirmed it was used solely as
a drug-trafficking logistics base.

foreign nationals had lived and worked at the house for over a year.

province but their Bangkok business was illegal. Operating without local
authorisation carries a maximum penalty of one year in prison or a 20,000-baht
fine. Police sent the seized cannabis to a laboratory to determine whether

The Ingulskyi District Court of Mykolaiv sentenced a local man to nine years in
prison for growing cannabis on his household plot and storing dried, crushed
narcotic material in the attic of his house. He was 51 years old and had
cultivated the cannabis since April 2026. The court found him guilty on
both charges and imposed nine years without confiscation of property. The
court noted that he had already served a five-year prison sentence for growing
cannabis.

kilograms of cannabis that had been stored in the attic. The prosecutor's
office likewise reported 14 plants and more than 8 kilograms of cannabis found
during the July search. The police statement gave a higher figure, saying
officers seized over 10 kilograms of dried narcotic raw material, while the
prosecutor reported more than 8 kilograms of cannabis. Police said the man
carefully tended the plants on his plot, fertilising the soil, weeding and
watering them regularly. He dried part of the harvest in the house attic
and crushed and packed the rest into glass jars for storage and, according to
investigators, sale.

Officers from police department No. 2 of the Mykolaiv district police identified
the activity in July, detained the man and notified him of suspicion of
producing and storing drugs for sale and of cultivating cannabis. During
the trial he admitted growing cannabis and making a narcotic substance but said
it was for personal use; the court rejected that claim as an attempt to avoid
responsibility. The court ordered the seized cannabis and plants destroyed
and recovered 28,400 hryvnias in expert-examination costs from him. The
verdict has not yet taken legal effect.
